Peres Jepchirchir won the 2026 Sydney marathon by three minutes and 40 seconds

Reigning world marathon champion Peres Jepchirchir has been banned for three years for a doping violation.

The 33-year-old, who also won Olympic gold in 2021, was provisionally suspended by the Athletics Integrity Unit (AIU) in October after an out-of-competition sample tested positive for erythropoietin (EPO).

The sample was collected in Kenya prior to Jepchirchir winning the Sydney Marathon on 30 August 2026 and returned an adverse finding on 17 September.

She is one of three high-profile Kenyan athletes to have been sanctioned. Veronica Loleo has also been banned for three years after admitting using EPO, while Ronald Korir has received a six-year ban after failing to explain abnormalities found in his biological passport.

EPO is a natural substance produced within the kidneys that stimulates the creation of new red blood cells.

If injected, it increases the amount of red blood cells, which carry oxygen to the muscles, in the blood stream but is only detectable in urine or blood for a short window of time.

Jepchirchir's other major wins came at the New York Marathon in 2021, the Boston Marathon in 2022 and the London Marathon in 2024.

While she denied using EPO, she signed an admission of violations form and accepted disqualification of all her competitive results since 17 July 2026.

"The Kenyan authorities have made a lot of progress in the fight against doping in the last five years, but these cases highlight that there is still a long way to go," said Brett Clothier, chief executive of the AIU.

"The Kenyan government is aware of the current situation and has committed to further strengthen the Anti-Doping Agency of Kenya and take action to address the criminal networks that facilitate doping within the country.

"We will discuss the details behind these commitments with the Kenyan government in the coming months."

South African DJ Lag says it is a "dream come true" to have his music featured on Grand Theft Auto 6 (GTA 6), the hugely popular video game released on Thursday.

DJ lag, one of South Africa's best-known electronic music producers, is among several African stars to feature, alongside Nigerian singers Burna Boy and Asake.

"I can't explain the feeling. I started playing the game last night and it's amazing," DJ Lag told the BBC's Newsday programme, adding that he had been playing GTA since he was about 10 years old and could hardly believe he was now part of the latest edition.

Many players have already had a chance to play the game following its worldwide launch .

The game, which lets players explore a fictional American city, features a dedicated African music radio station playing Afrobeats, amapiano and other sounds from across the continent.

The release of GTA 6 ends a 13-year wait for a new edition of the game.

GTA 6 is a satirical video series associated with crime and violence

Rockstar Games, the developer behind the franchise, has revealed details of the game's soundtrack and some in-game radio stations, but has yet to release a complete list of songs featured in the game.

Rockstar says AfroBank FM features everything from 20th Century African classics to contemporary amapiano and 3-step, giving the continent's music a prominent place in the latest edition.

Burna Boy co-hosts the station alongside British DJ and producer Palms Trax, while Asake's hit song Joha is among the tracks players can listen to as they drive around the game's virtual world.

DJ Lag, whose real name is Lwazi Asanda Gwala, is regarded as one of the pioneers of gqom, a genre of electronic dance music that emerged in the port city of Durban in the early 2010s.

Ghanaian highlife legends Pat Thomas and Ebo Taylor also feature, alongside South African artists Robot Boii and Kamo Mphela, bringing a mix of classic and contemporary African music to one of gaming's biggest franchises.

Rockstar has also announced a 34-track official soundtrack album, released in partnership with Atlantic Records, featuring an original Burna Boy song titled Bigger.

For African fans, the inclusion of familiar music adds another dimension to the experience, allowing players to hear some of the continent's biggest sounds while exploring the American setting.

The series allows players to roam through sprawling fictional cities, drive vehicles and complete missions involving crime, police pursuits and other adventures.

The latest instalment takes players to Vice City, a fictional version of Miami, and the surrounding US state of Leonida, inspired by Florida.

Its story follows two criminals, Jason and Lucia, who become caught up in a wider conspiracy after a robbery goes wrong.

The launch has generated enormous excitement among gamers around the world.

Some fans downloaded it in advance so they could begin playing as soon as it became available, while others have booked leave from work.

The previous edition, GTA 5, was one of the best-selling video games of all time, selling more than 200 million copies worldwide.

The new release is expected to be another major commercial success, although it remains to be seen whether it will match its predecessor's extraordinary sales.

The assistant referee had a 60-day recovery period after being operated on

An Ecuadorian footballer has been banned for eight years for throwing a rock at an assistant referee, leaving him requiring surgery to his face.

Jhon Perlaza was playing for Club Ciudad de Yantzaza against Club Rio Aguarico FC in a third-tier match in October when the incident took place.

The stone struck assistant referee Lenin Giovanni Ojeda Nunez in the face in the 96th minute of the game, which was subsequently abandoned.

A video on social media shows Perlaza standing up in the team's dugout to throw the stone, with Nunez instantly falling to the floor and holding his face after the object hits him. He then receives medical attention.

"The assistant referee suffered serious injuries that required surgery and a 60-day recovery period," the Ecuadorian Football Federation (FEF) said.

"The disciplinary committee found the player responsible for physical aggression against a match official and suspended him for eight years from all football-related activity, until 19 October, 2034.

"In addition, the FEF will ask Fifa to extend this sanction worldwide."

The FEF also fined his club Yantzaza $2,000 (£1,521) and ordered them to pay Nunez's medical fees of $4,369 (£3,323).

In a statement released on 20 October, three days after the match, Yantzaza apologised to the refereeing team and the fans, and confirmed Perlaza had been sacked as a result of the incident.

"As an institution, we categorically reject all acts of aggression, whether verbal or physical, both inside and outside sporting venues. We firmly believe that football should be a space of respect, coexistence, and fair play," they said.

"Once the person responsible for this regrettable incident was identified, the institution made the decision to remove him immediately, and he is therefore no longer part of our club."

Itororokanirizo ry'amakuru AFP rimusubiramwo, yagize ati: "Umuntu ari ku nkengera z'ikiyaga yarashobora kwumva amaborogo y'abantu bari muri ubwo bwato."

AFP yatangaje ko umwe mu barokotse iryo sanganya abajijwe n'abapolisi yavuze ko ubwo bwato bwari butwaye abantu bashika 100.

Abapolisi basanze mu bisigarira vy'ubwo bwato impapuro ndangamuntu, amaterefone ngendanwa menshi hamwe n'ibindi vyari bitunze abari muri bwo. Muri ivyo, harimwo n'igikoresho co kw'ishure bikekwa ko cari ic'umunyeshure yiga mu mashure yisumbuye.

Amakuru ya BBC Gahuza ako kanya kuri WhatsApp yawe

Mu nama y'abashikiranganji yabaye ku musi wa gatatu, Perezida Diomaye Faye yagaragaje impungenge ku bijanye n'ukwiyongera kw'ingendo zitemewe z'abimukira bava muri Sénégal, bizeye gushika i Buraya.

Yasavye ubushikiranganji bw'intwaro yo hagati gutegura icegeranyo gisuzuma imvo zituma abantu bafata izo ngendo zitera akaga, kikerekana n'ingingo zoshobora gufatwa kugira ico kibazo gitorerwe umuti.

Inyuma y'irindi sanganya ry'ubwato ryabaye mu kwezi guheze, Faye yari yahamagariye abanya Sénégal kutishira mu kaga ko guhitanwa n'urupfu mu kugerageza kujabuka ikiyaga.

Abantu ibihumbi n'ibihumbi bo muri Afrika yo mu Burengero baramaze gupfa canke bakaburwa irengero bariko bagerageza guhunga intambara, intwaro z'agahotoro canke ubukene.

Ishirahamwe mpuzamakungu rijejwe abimukira (IOM) ryavuze mu kwezi guheze ko ryari rimaze kwandika abantu nibura 454 bapfuye canke babuzwe irengero muri uyu mwaka gusa, bariko bagerageza guca mw'ibahari Atlantique, hafi y'inkengera zo mu Burengero bwa Afrika.

Iryo shirahamwe ryagabishije ko ico gitigiri gishobora kuba kiri munsi y'ic'ukuri, kuko hari ubwato bwinshi buzama ntihagire umuntu n'umwe arokoka canke ngo hasigare ikimenyetso na kimwe c'ivyabashikiye.

The band have become known for their energetic live performances and interwoven four-part harmonies

Westside Cowboy have been announced as BBC Introducing Artist of the Year 2026.

Jimmy Bradbury, Reuben Haycocks, Aoife Anson O'Connell and Paddy Murphy formed the band in Manchester in 2023 and have since rocketed from the pub circuit to some of the UK's biggest festivals.

The award is presented to an up-and-coming artist or band who has, with the support of BBC Introducing, made a significant impact and has previously been won by Olivia Dean, Myles Smith and Tom Grennan.

Murphy, from Longridge in Lancashire, said the win put them in "good company", with Bradbury, from Shropshire, adding that it was "very flattering".

BBC Introducing supports new musical talent across the UK , providing a platform to propel new artists on to the local and national stage through 30 Introducing shows, three national radio shows and six shows across BBC Radio 1, Radio 1Xtra, Radio 2, 6Music, Radio 3 and Asian Network.

About 72,000 tracks from emerging UK artists supported by BBC Introducing make it on to the airwaves each year.

Westside Cowboy uploaded their debut single I've Never Met Anyone I Thought I Could Really Love (Until I Met You) to the Introducing platform in November 2024 and had their first play on radio within hours.

Murphy and Bradbury were surprised with the award during a radio interview

The four-piece played in various other bands before coming together to form Westside Cowboy.

Haycocks, O'Connell, and Murphy had met at Manchester's Royal Northern College of Music in 2021 and later got to know Bradbury after meeting him in the nearby Johnny Roadhouse music shop.

Murphy and Bradbury played in surf-rock trio Katz, while Murphy and Haycocks both worked together in noise-pop trio, DieKaiDie, but it was when Bradbury, who was working in the music shop repairing guitars, asked the others if they wanted to start a new band that Westside Cowboy's journey began.

By the time their second single, Shells, was released in April 2025, they had been been selected to play the BBC Introducing stage at Glastonbury Festival, and the song was put on the BBC 6Music playlist.

Their meteoric rise saw seen them appear on BBC music show Later... with Jools Holland in June and their debut album It Goes On was released on Island Records in August, peaking at number five in the UK charts.

Westside Cowboy reminisced about the early days on BBC Radio Manchester

Thanking the Introducing network and listeners for their support, Murphy said it was "really cool to be recognised for the music you make".

"We say this a lot, so apologies if we sound like a broken record, [but] it's funny with this band because... we started it with so little pretence or plan," he said.

"So whenever people give us something cool like [this award], it's all a bit surreal because it still feels like a weekend project that we now just get to do way more regularly.

"We're very lucky it's one of those things.

Westside Cowboy formed in 2023, having played together in other bands

William Wolstenholme, presenter and producer of BBC Introducing in Lancashire & Cumbria, gave the band their first play and said he remembers messaging them to upload the track.

"Over the past two years, Westside Cowboy have become surely the most exciting band in Manchester, and therefore the country," he said.

"They've fast-tracked from the sweaty pubs of the city's student music scene to many of the most famous venues in the country.

"It's a rise whose speed can scarcely be believed, and one that has shocked much of the music industry."

He said the band's obvious camaraderie was one of their main selling points.

"They're still the same four mates wandering down Oxford Road in Manchester, and the reason the music has resonated with so many people is because it's a true reflection of those four kids," he said.

"They've been themselves and, in doing so, have brought the fashion and style of the past 10 years of UK post-punk culture down to earth."

Ni ibyaha yakoreye i Nyanza mu Ntara y'Amajyepfo, abatangabuhamya babajijwe bakaba baragarutse cyane kuri bariyeli yari i Nyanza hafi y'ahitwa kwa Premier, hiciwe abatutsi benshi aho Madjaliwa ashinjwa kubigiramo uruhare.

Ashinjwa uruhare mu rupfu rw'abantu batandukanye ndetse by'umwihariko mu bwicanyi bwibasiye Abakono.

Umutangabuhamya Florent Piton ni we mutangabuhamya wasobanuye amakuru atuma Jenoside yakorewe Abatutsi yumvikana, temoin de contexte.

Yerekanye ko kwica Abatutsi byatangiye mu 1959, biza kuba Jenoside mu 1994.

Mu ba avoka bahagarariye abarega - parties civiles, Emma Sabadotto yagaragaje ko mu myumvire ishingiye ku macakubiri yerekeye abagore b’Abatutsi, harimo igitekerezo cy’uko bagira imiterere y’umubiri utemba itoto, bakagira n'uburanga butangaje bukurura abagabo.

Umutangabuhamya yahise yerekeza ku nomero ya 6 y’ikinyamakuru KANGURA, yasohoye “Amategeko Icumi y’Abahutu” (Les dix commandements des Bahutu). Muri ayo mategeko, harimo irivuga ko:

“Abahutu batagomba kugwa mu mutego w’abagore b’Abatutsi bashobora kuyobya abagabo b’Abahutu, bakoresheje ubwiza n’uburanga bwabo kugira ngo babigarurire, babatere gushyigikira inyungu z’Abatutsi.”

Yasoje asobanura ko iki kimenyetso gifasha kugaragaza ko ifatwa ku ngufu ryakorewe abagore b’Abatutsi ryari kimwe mu bigize umugambi wa Jenoside. Aha, yerekana ko iryo fatwa ku ngufu ryatijwe umurindi n'iyo sura bari barambitse umugore wo mu bwoko bw'Abatutsi.

Impuzamashyirahamwe y’Umupira w’Amaguru ku Isi (FIFA) yatangaje ko yakiriye kandidatire ebyiri z’abifuza guhatana na Gianni Infantino ku mwanya wa Perezida w’uyu muryango mu matora ateganyijwe mu 2027. Abo ni Philippe Diallo ukomoka mu Bufaransa, uyobora Ishyirahamwe ry’Umupira w’Amaguru muri icyo gihugu (FFF), na Kohzo Tashima wo mu Buyapani, wahoze ayobora Ishyirahamwe ry’Umupira w’Amaguru muri icyo gihugu akaba uyu munsi ari Perezida waryo w’icyubahiro.

Aba bombi bazahatana na Gianni Infantino usanzwe ayobora FIFA kuva mu 2016, akaba ashaka kongera gutorerwa indi manda.

Amatora ateganyijwe ku wa 18 Werurwe 2027, azabera i Rabat muri Maroc, mu nama ya 77 ya FIFA izahuza abanyamuryango b’uyu muryango baturutse mu bihugu 211.

FIFA yatangaje ko kandidatire zatanzwe zashyikirijwe Komisiyo ishinzwe amatora kugira ngo zisuzumwe, harebwe niba abazitanze bujuje ibisabwa kugira ngo bemererwe kwiyamamaza. Umwanzuro wa nyuma ku bazemererwa kuzahatana uteganyijwe gutangazwa bitarenze ku wa 18 Gashyantare 2027.

Aya matora azaba afite umwihariko kuko Infantino agiye guhatanira kuyobora FIFA ahanganye n’abandi bakandida, mu gihe mu matora yo mu 2023 yari yiyamamaje nta wundi muhanganye. Kohzo Tashima na Philippe Diallo kandidatire zabo nizemezwa burundu, bazaba bafite akazi gakomeye ko guhangana na Infantino usanzwe afite ubunararibonye n’umubano ukomeye n’amashyirahamwe menshi y’umupira w’amaguru ku isi.

A consultant surgeon at Aberdeen Royal Infirmary has called for a corporate homicide investigation into claims of the unavoidable deaths of NHS Grampian patients over many years.

Dr Mohammed Habib, who is still a surgeon at the hospital, said he had been raising concerns for a decade, including with government ministers and police but he had been ignored.

The whistleblowing medic also leaked an unpublished expert review from 2022 which found 19 avoidable deaths among 45 patients in liver and pancreatic surgery, including some who bled to death in the operating theatre because of mistakes by surgeons.

The allegations come a week after a scathing report found poor leadership and culture at the NHS Grampian board. The board's management is yet to comment on these latest public claims.

Dr Mohammed Habib has been raising concerns for a decade

Last week, Healthcare Improvement Scotland (HIS) found "major deficiencies" across the region and revealed that a failure to learn from mistakes had caused "repeated and avoidable harm" to patients.

Health Secretary Angela Constance insisted that patients were safe and said she would demand "full transparency" at every level.

Habib, who has been a consultant with NHS Grampian since 2014, held a media conference on Thursday and said he was putting his career on the line to demand accountability from the health board.

The consultant said he formally reported serious concerns about dozens of avoidable deaths in 2021.

In 2024, he reported 20 cases from the previous decade to the police but no charges have been brought.

He has also leaked two reports by external experts which examined surgical care in NHS Grampian.

A 2022 review looked at 45 patients in the care of liver and pancreatic services at Aberdeen Royal Infirmary (ARI) between 2015 and 2021.

It said 31 had died, and 19 of them were considered to have died of avoidable consequences of surgery or intervention.

The 2022 review criticised decision-making in liver surgery for occasionally being "overly aggressive", with surgery going ahead even if the disease was thought to be inoperable.

In pancreatic surgery, patients were regularly rushed into theatre without adequate planning or consideration of non-surgical alternatives, the experts said.

The review said blood losses in both surgeries was "unacceptably high" and said there was a lack of leadership and no clear standards for planning before operations.

It said poor decision-making and aggressive strategies were adopted despite high levels of deaths being predicted.

A second report earlier earlier this year raised similar themes, with poor judgement about the risks and benefits of operating and repeated examples of massive blood losses and deaths during and after surgery.

It said it was clear that problems in the unit were "long standing and recurrent", adding that NHS Grampian had tried to improve outcomes but had not made the structural changes needed.

It noted that the unit did not have enough specialist staff to deliver the service safely, and that despite concerns being raised repeatedly since 2010, the issues had not been dealt with.

It strongly recommended that no complex or major HPB (Hepatopancreatobiliary) surgery should take place at Aberdeen Royal Infirmary.

Dr Habib, who has worked in General Surgery & HPB (liver, pancreas and bile duct) since 2014, said he thought several hundred patients had come to harm from an excessively high rate of complications.

He said he had tried his best to use the whistleblowing procedures but the institutions he had contacted had failed to act as robustly as they should have.

He said he first became about avoidable surgery-related deaths in 2016.

In July 2021, he formally raised serious concerns about what he believes were dozens of avoidable deaths.

In February 2024, he spoke to Police Scotland.

Habib said he believes NHS Grampian was guilty of "wicked recklessness and an indifference to patient deaths".

The consultant said the 2022 external expert report, which was never made public, concluded that 19 deaths out of a case study of 45 were avoidable (42%).

He said he had contacted the first minister and health secretary on numerous occasions since June 2023 but the Scottish government had said it had "no jurisdiction" to investigate whistleblowing claims.

Habib also said that the Independent Whistleblowing Officer (INWO) refused to progress his complaints on the basis that they were either "time barred".

He also wrote to the chief executive of NHS Grampian, Laura Skaife Knight, in December 2025.

She replied: "I would be grateful if you can let HIS complete it enquiries rather than continuing to correspond with me about these matters, as I have nothing further to add to this response at this stage."

Habib said: "They are avoiding accountability by not being transparent about what damage has been done, while promising heaven and earth going forward."

Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni and Tanzanian President Samia Suluhu Hassan have agreed to accelerate preparations for a Standard Gauge Railway that would connect Isaka in Tanzania to Mpondwe, on Uganda’s border with the Democratic Republic of Congo.

The leaders witnessed the signing of a framework agreement at State House in Entebbe on November 18, during Hassan’s two-day state visit.

The proposed line would pass through Lusahunga and Murongo/Kikagati before reaching Mpondwe. The presidents said it could improve regional trade, cut transport costs and open a new rail gateway to eastern DRC.

They directed their governments to speed up feasibility studies, technical designs and financing plans. The project’s cost and construction timetable have not yet been established.

The railway is planned to reach the Ugandan border; onward rail links into eastern DRC would be needed to connect the Congolese market directly.

Earlier tripartite discussions and a route survey involving Uganda, Tanzania and DRC laid groundwork for the proposal, with the African Development Bank supporting project preparation.

For Tanzania, the line could extend the Central Corridor and strengthen the role of Dar es Salaam port. Uganda would gain another route to regional markets and a potential corridor for goods moving between DRC and the coast.

The railway is part of wider Uganda–Tanzania infrastructure cooperation. The leaders also welcomed progress on the 1,443-kilometre East African Crude Oil Pipeline, which they reported was 93.9% complete, and called for the development of Tanga as a regional energy hub.

Simba Supermarket has opened its 16th branch in Kabuga, continuing its expansion as it seeks to bring its services to more communities across Rwanda.

Patrice Ndanga, Executive Secretary of Rusororo Sector, attended the opening and presented Simba Suppermarket with a trophy in recognition of the company’s corporate social responsibility work in the area.

The Kabuga launch follows several recent additions to Simba’s network. The company opened its 13th branch in Rubavu in March 2025, complementing its Musanze outlet, and has also expanded in Kigali, including in Gahanga and Nyamirambo.

Its branches sell groceries, fresh produce, bakery items and household goods, and the company also offers online shopping.

Speaking on Thursday, chief executive Teklay Teame said Rwanda’s business environment was helping the company grow. “The business environment created by our government is helping us expand,” he said.

The expansion comes after a fire swept through GOICO Plaza in Musanze in October. Simba’s branch was spared, and all staff were safe.

Rwanda is stepping up efforts to attract high-spending international visitors and strengthen its position as a premium tourism destination through its participation in Luxperience 2026, a luxury travel trade event taking place in Sydney, Australia, from November 17 to 20.

The four-day event brings together leading luxury tourism buyers, travel advisors and industry players from Australia, New Zealand and other international markets, offering the country an opportunity to promote its exclusive travel experiences and establish business relationships with influential players in the global tourism industry.

The delegation is led by Rwanda Development Board (RDB) Chief Tourism Officer Irène Murerwa and includes local tour operators and travel agents, in collaboration with the Rwandan High Commission in Singapore.

Their participation is aimed at showcasing the country’s high-end tourism offerings, attracting new travel partnerships and increasing its visibility among affluent travellers across the Asia-Pacific region.

Rwanda has increasingly positioned itself as a luxury tourism destination, building its appeal around high-end accommodation, wildlife experiences, conservation tourism and personalised travel services.

Among its flagship attractions is gorilla trekking in Volcanoes National Park, an experience that draws international visitors willing to pay premium prices for close encounters with endangered mountain gorillas in their natural habitat.

Other experiences include wildlife safaris in Akagera National Park, chimpanzee tracking and canopy walks in Nyungwe National Park, as well as leisure and cultural tourism around Lake Kivu.

By presenting these experiences to international luxury travel buyers, the delegation hopes to encourage travel companies to include the destination in their premium holiday packages and recommend it to clients seeking exclusive and distinctive African experiences.

The participation also carries significant economic opportunities for the country.

Australia, New Zealand and the wider Asia-Pacific region represent potential source markets for visitors who can contribute to tourism revenues through premium accommodation, guided excursions, domestic transport, hospitality and other tourism-related services.

Securing partnerships with established international travel advisors could help generate more bookings, increase visitor spending and extend the benefits of tourism to local businesses, including hotels, tour operators, transport providers, restaurants and community-based tourism initiatives.

The expansion into these markets could also help diversify the country’s international visitor base, reducing its reliance on traditional source markets while strengthening its competitiveness in the global luxury travel industry.

Beyond attracting visitors, international exposure at events such as Luxperience provides an opportunity to build confidence among overseas travel companies and position the country as a destination capable of delivering high-quality, personalised and sustainable tourism experiences.

The involvement of local tour operators and travel agents is also important in ensuring that international partnerships translate into direct business opportunities for domestic tourism companies.

Through its tourism promotion strategy, the country has continued to prioritise high-value, low-impact tourism, with conservation and premium visitor experiences forming key pillars of its approach.

Participation in Luxperience 2026 therefore offers another opportunity to connect its tourism ambitions with international demand, particularly among travellers seeking exclusive wildlife encounters, nature-based holidays and luxury experiences in Africa.
